title: Completions along two ideals each containing a power of the other agree
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I,J\subseteq A$ ideals and $c,d\ge1$ integers with $I^c\subseteq J$ and $J^d\subseteq I$. Let $M$ be an $A$-module, $M^\wedge_I=\varprojlim_nM/I^nM$ and $M^\wedge_J=\varprojlim_nM/J^nM$ (compatible sequences, componentwise $A$-module structure), with canonical maps $\iota_I:M\to M^\wedge_I$, $\iota_J:M\to M^\wedge_J$, $x\mapsto(x\bmod I^nM)_n$ resp. $(x\bmod J^nM)_n$. Then the map $\theta:M^\wedge_J\to M^\wedge_I$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto(x_{dk}\bmod I^kM)_k$ (well defined since $J^{dk}M\subseteq I^kM$) is an isomorphism of $A$-modules with inverse $(y_k)_k\mapsto(y_{cn}\bmod J^nM)_n$ (well defined since $I^{cn}M\subseteq J^nM$), and $\theta\circ\iota_J=\iota_I$. In particular $M$ is $I$-adically complete ($\iota_I$ bijective) if and only if it is $J$-adically complete. For $M=A$ (where $M^\wedge_I=\varprojlim_nA/I^n$ with componentwise multiplication) $\theta$ is an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, line 22806); proof: the systems of maps M/I^nM -> M/J^{floor(n/c)}M and M/J^mM -> M/I^{floor(m/d)}M give mutually inverse maps of the completions

proof.text: Inclusions of submodules. For $k\ge0$: $J^{dk}=(J^d)^k\subseteq I^k$ (since $J^d\subseteq I$ and powers of ideals are monotone), hence $J^{dk}M\subseteq I^kM$; likewise $I^{cn}=(I^c)^n\subseteq J^n$, hence $I^{cn}M\subseteq J^nM$. So there are surjective $A$-linear quotient maps $\pi^{JI}_k:M/J^{dk}M\to M/I^kM$ and $\pi^{IJ}_n:M/I^{cn}M\to M/J^nM$, $x\bmod(\cdot)\mapsto x\bmod(\cdot)$. Any composite of such reductions $M/N_1\to M/N_2\to M/N_3$ along inclusions $N_1\subseteq N_2\subseteq N_3$ of submodules is the reduction $M/N_1\to M/N_3$ (both send $x\bmod N_1$ to $x\bmod N_3$); this is used below without further mention.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: $\theta$ and $\psi$ are well defined. Let $(x_n)_n\in M^\wedge_J$, i.e. $x_n\in M/J^nM$ with $x_{n'}\bmod J^nM=x_n$ for $n\le n'$. Put $y_k=\pi^{JI}_k(x_{dk})=x_{dk}\bmod I^kM$. For $k\le k'$: $y_{k'}\bmod I^kM=x_{dk'}\bmod I^kM=(x_{dk'}\bmod J^{dk}M)\bmod I^kM=x_{dk}\bmod I^kM=y_k$, using $J^{dk}M\subseteq I^kM$ and compatibility of $(x_n)$ for $dk\le dk'$. So $\theta((x_n)_n)=(y_k)_k\in M^\wedge_I$. Symmetrically, for $(y_k)_k\in M^\wedge_I$ the family $\psi((y_k)_k)=(y_{cn}\bmod J^nM)_n$ is compatible (for $n\le n'$: $y_{cn'}\bmod J^nM=(y_{cn'}\bmod I^{cn}M)\bmod J^nM=y_{cn}\bmod J^nM$), so $\psi:M^\wedge_I\to M^\wedge_J$ is defined. (Stacks uses the equivalent systems $M/I^nM\to M/J^{\lfloor n/c\rfloor}M$, $M/J^mM\to M/I^{\lfloor m/d\rfloor}M$; the reindexing by $dk$, $cn$ in the statement gives the same maps on the limits, by compatibility.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: $\theta$ and $\psi$ are $A$-linear: the $A$-module structures of $M^\wedge_I$, $M^\wedge_J$ are componentwise, and each component of $\theta$ (resp. $\psi$) is the composite of the projection $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_{dk}$ (resp. $(y_k)_k\mapsto y_{cn}$), which is $A$-linear, with the $A$-linear quotient map $\pi^{JI}_k$ (resp. $\pi^{IJ}_n$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: $\psi\circ\theta=\mathrm{id}$. For $(x_n)_n\in M^\wedge_J$ and $n\ge0$, the $n$-th component of $\psi(\theta((x_n)))$ is $(x_{d\cdot cn}\bmod I^{cn}M)\bmod J^nM=x_{dcn}\bmod J^nM$ (reduction along $J^{dcn}M\subseteq I^{cn}M\subseteq J^nM$), and since $n\le dcn$ ($c,d\ge1$) compatibility of $(x_n)$ gives $x_{dcn}\bmod J^nM=x_n$. $\theta\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}$. For $(y_k)_k\in M^\wedge_I$ and $k\ge0$, the $k$-th component of $\theta(\psi((y_k)))$ is $(y_{c\cdot dk}\bmod J^{dk}M)\bmod I^kM=y_{cdk}\bmod I^kM=y_k$ since $k\le cdk$. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules with inverse $\psi$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: $\theta\circ\iota_J=\iota_I$. For $x\in M$, $\iota_J(x)=(x\bmod J^nM)_n$, and $\theta(\iota_J(x))_k=(x\bmod J^{dk}M)\bmod I^kM=x\bmod I^kM=\iota_I(x)_k$. Consequently $\psi\circ\iota_I=\psi\circ\theta\circ\iota_J=\iota_J$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: Completeness. Since $\iota_I=\theta\circ\iota_J$ with $\theta$ bijective, $\iota_I$ is bijective if and only if $\iota_J$ is ($\iota_J=\psi\circ\iota_I$ with $\psi=\theta^{-1}$). So $M$ is $I$-adically complete iff it is $J$-adically complete (completeness meaning bijectivity of the canonical map, as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] for $M=A$ and in the statement for modules).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0319 (lemma-change-ideal-completion, lines 22805-22822) and its proof

proof.text: Ring isomorphism for $M=A$. Then $I^kM=I^k$, $J^nM=J^n$, and $M^\wedge_I=\varprojlim_kA/I^k$, $M^\wedge_J=\varprojlim_nA/J^n$ are the completion rings of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] with componentwise operations. Each component of $\theta$ is the projection to $A/J^{dk}$ (a ring map, operations being componentwise) followed by the quotient map $A/J^{dk}\to A/I^k$, which is a ring homomorphism since $J^{dk}\subseteq I^k$. So $\theta$ preserves $1$ and products; being an additive bijection (previous steps), it is a ring isomorphism, with inverse the ring map $\psi$.

lean.statement: theorem changeIdealCompletion {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A) (c d : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hIJ : I ^ c ≤ J) (hJI : J ^ d ≤ I) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] : ∃ (θ : AdicCompletion J M ≃ₗ[A] AdicCompletion I M), (∀ (x : AdicCompletion J M) (k : ℕ), (θ x).val k = Submodule.factor (show J ^ (d * k) • (⊤ : Submodule A M) ≤ I ^ k • (⊤ : Submodule A M) by exact powerReductionJI I J d k M hJI) (x.val (d * k))) ∧ (∀ (x : AdicCompletion I M) (n : ℕ), (θ.symm x).val n = Submodule.factor (show I ^ (c * n) • (⊤ : Submodule A M) ≤ J ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M) by exact powerReductionIJ I J c n M hIJ) (x.val (c * n))) ∧ (∀ (x : M), θ (AdicCompletion.of J M x) = AdicCompletion.of I M x) ∧ (Function.Bijective (AdicCompletion.of I M) ↔ Function.Bijective (AdicCompletion.of J M))
